text: {"memo": "As of the 2025-03-31 research note, Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) reported FY2024 results. FY2024 net sales were about $638 billion, up roughly 12% from $575 billion in FY2023. FY2024 operating income was about $68.6 billion, and net income was about $59.2 billion, or $6.31 per diluted share. Operating margin expanded to about 10.8% from 5.3% in FY2023; net margin was about 9.3%. Cash flow from operations was about $108 billion, with free cash flow perhaps around $77 billion. AWS revenue was about $67.4 billion for FY2024, and AWS operating income was about $29.8 billion. In FY2023, revenue was $574.8 billion, up 9% year over year, with operating income of about $30.4 billion and net income of about $30.4 billion, or $3.08 per share. FY2022 revenue was $513.9 billion, up 9%, but the company had an operating loss of about $2.8 billion and a net loss of about $2.7 billion, or $0.33 per share. The business showed a strong recovery and operating leverage, with FY2024 profit more than doubling from FY2023. The stock should trade on AWS growth, retail margins, and capex. View: AMZN remains a premium mega-cap compounder, but valuation and competition limit near-term upside."}
